hook: Fake 'bank managers' take *₹2.28 crore* from Kukatpally family
hook_b: Fake 'bank managers' take *₹2.28 crore* from Kukatpally family
tldr: A 61-year-old software professional and his son lost ₹2.28 crore after being added to WhatsApp investment groups and shown fake bank ID cards.

beats.what: The father was added to two WhatsApp groups and contacted by women claiming to be private bank relationship managers.
beats.why: They showed real SEBI registration details of genuine bank-linked entities, so the platforms looked real.
beats.care: Anyone in WhatsApp 'investment circles' is a target; real banks don't ask you to trade on links they send.

event.label: Fake bank staff push trading app

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: The victims opened 'direct market access' accounts on a website and app the fraudsters set up. A case was registered on Tuesday for cheating, personation and forgery.

cards.q: Who should block fake investment WhatsApp groups?

qs: How can someone check if a WhatsApp 'relationship manager' really works for a bank?

facts.t: Telangana lost *₹50 crore* to 'digital arrest' scams in 10 months.

steps.e: Fake bank staff show ID cards, SEBI details
Money moved to accounts on fake app

viz.verdict: A layered trust trick that used real registration details.

learn.t: DMA = direct market access, a trading account; fraudsters use the term to sound official

watch: Whether police trace the bank accounts the money went to.

sources.name: Times of India
sources.title: Fake bank officials lure Hyderabad techie, son into ₹2 crore stock investment fraud

fact: WhatsApp stock 'advisers' posing as bank staff took *₹2.28 crore* from a Kukatpally family
twist: When the son tried to withdraw, fraudsters demanded 'taxes'; he paid *₹22.92 lakh* more.
